bits.stat: Dropped about 3,100 times by more than 130 different people. The most-used emoji in the server.
bits.def: Your ticket to the phone. PLA is the Phone Losers of America, RBCP's crew and half the room's home base. Drop the PLA bell in chat and you're in line. The bot calls your name when it's your turn, and you'd better be in voice when it does.

quote.text: If you want to make a call, put a PLA bell emoji in chat.

bits.stat: Said by more than 30 different people. Written into the very first rules.
bits.def: The reveal. When a call has gone as far as it can go, you tell them who they've been talking to: 101.1 The Butt. They have just been buttslammed. Optional, never required, and never a reason to leak where the call is coming from.

quote.text: No leaking the source of the call to the people we're calling.

bits.stat: The station behind every reveal since night one.
bits.def: The radio station the Callective claims to be when it's time to come clean. Callers like to add a proud on-air confession about what kind of listener they are. Nobody has ever asked for the frequency to be checked.

quote.text: If you want to reveal that it's a prank, we are 101.1 The Butt and "You just got buttslammed".

bits.stat: Still in the rules two years later. Brought up by 17 different people.
bits.def: The one rule that has never needed rewording. Be as rude as you want to the person you called, but if you're drunk and abusive to the room, you're off the phone. Drunk and charming is a gray area.

quote.text: If you don't know why I have to put this here, YOU are why I have to put this here.

bits.stat: Said by nearly 50 different people. Has its own emoji.
bits.def: The most dangerous word on a Callective call. Every escalation runs through it: polite at first, then firm, then shouted in all caps. When a caller says it in the right tone, chat fires off the ma'am emoji like a sports crowd.

bits.stat: Talked about by 47 different people. The most-called kind of place on the show.
bits.def: Hotels are the Callective's home stadium. The front desk, the room number, the ice machine, the lost and found, the hot tub: half the premises in history start with someone at a hotel who has a problem only the night clerk can solve.

bits.stat: Rated by 41 different people.
bits.def: When a caller puts the other person on hold, they play their own music, and the room reviews it like a record label. Good hold music is a point of pride. Some regulars have a signature track.

bits.stat: Called out by 18 different people since the first week.
bits.def: If anyone talks behind the person you called, the room hears it, fixates on it, and demands the caller tell that guy to be quiet. In later years it became the wife, the coworker, or whoever else is lurking off-mic.

bits.stat: Joined by 34 different people. Peaked in summer 2026.
bits.def: One themed call that everyone in voice can jump into at once. Somebody calls it in the queue, the line pauses, and the whole room piles onto one poor person on the other end. Once you call an all call, you can't take it back.

bits.stat: Declared by 13 different people.
bits.def: A caller announces they're having a fart attack, usually at a hotel, and the room supplies the sound effects. It has been used to get attention, to end a call, and once as a distraction from a dog giving birth.

bits.stat: Brought up by more than 60 different people. Peaks every September.
bits.def: Notes left on parked cars saying sorry, I dinged your car, call me. The number rings the crew, who answer live. September is Dingtember, the whole month is dings, and chat spends it inventing new things to have dinged the car with.

bits.stat: 20 different people in on it. Peaked in December 2025.
bits.def: Before a Five Below call, chat posts a shopping list in spoiler tags. The caller clicks one blind and asks the store for whatever it says, with a straight face. Keeping a straight face has never once been achieved.

bits.stat: 29 different people have hit it.
bits.def: The gym alarm that goes off when someone grunts too loud. A Callective premise, an animated emoji, and the thing the chat reaches for whenever a call gets too intense.

bits.stat: Mentioned by 29 different people, nearly 175 times.
bits.def: The official mumble rapper of the Callective. Yo Ghost turns up in the queue, on calls, and in chat, where everyone asks for one more verse about ghosts and aliens.

bits.stat: Said by 18 different people, mostly yelling it.
bits.def: A clip of a very angry man from a call that went a bit viral around the community and turned into a catchphrase. If someone types it in chat, everyone else types it back.

bits.stat: Started as a call character. Now he runs the queue.
bits.def: First a character in calls by RBCP and CrieFaux. Now the name of the bot that runs the queue, greets everyone who joins voice, and moves the line along like a mall cop with a schedule.

quote.text: Alright, Cyber's finished. I got a badge and I'm usin' it — NEXT.

bits.stat: Chanted by 12 different people.
bits.def: Dr. Tom Servo's other self. When Tom Man gets on the phone, chat chants it. He has opinions about who owns the roof.

bits.stat: Has a fan club of 11 and counting.
bits.def: GreenImp's duck. Quacks along on calls, has a fan club in chat, and pulls better numbers than some hosts.

bits.stat: Cawed by more than 20 different people.
bits.def: Any time a crow comes up, on a call or in chat, the room answers with caw. It started in January 2025 and it has not stopped.

bits.stat: Has come up with 14 different people.
bits.def: Every so often, chat breaks the sad news that Carrot Top has died, or that he's checking into the hotel being called. Neither is true. Chat will not stop.

bits.stat: Brought up by 19 different people.
bits.def: RBCP's long-running Phone Losers of America show, the longest-running prank show in the community. A lot of Callective regulars came from it, the ding number turns up in its episodes, and RBCP hosts the Callective too.

bits.stat: Not ours. We just say it sometimes.
bits.def: A Bonerhaus thing that wanders into the Callective now and then, since the show is a mix of PLA and Prankcast folks. If someone tells you good job, pig boy, it's a compliment. Probably.

lines: The host will be the only person permitted to speak initially. Everybody else is muted (including the soundboard, you scamp). So, no yelling things from the sidelines.
The host will unmute people one at a time to do a prank call. Prank calls will be done purely on a voluntary basis, so you'll only go when you feel you are ready.
When making calls, we follow the rules of prank calling and the server. Calls should be wacky and fun, not abusive to the people we call.
Remember, sometimes calls just don't work out and it's nobody's fault. Let's all be supportive.
If you're just drunk and abusive, you will be removed from calls and/or timed out in chat. If you don't know why I have to put this here, YOU are why I have to put this here.
Efforts will be made to make things as fair as possible when it comes to turns.
No leaking the source of the call to the people we're calling. If you want to reveal that it's a prank, we are 101.1 The Butt and "You just got buttslammed".
